title.narrative: Explosive Ordnance Risk Education for IDPs, Returnees and Refugees in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe States of Northeast Nigeria

description.narrative:
Established in 1997, the United Nations Mine Action Service (UNMAS) leads, coordinates, and implements projects and programmes to mitigate the threats posed by explosive ordnance to the benefit of millions of people worldwide.

UNMAS delivers Explosive Ordnance Risk Education to affected populations, including IDPs, host communities, returnees and refugees. Awareness materials, radio messages and pre-recorded messages in talking devices are designed to the specific context of Northeast Nigeria and to the specific needs of each gender and age group. 

UNOPS works with UNMAS to address the threat of landmines and unexploded ordnance.
